name: Kiwi
description: Kiwi is an exceptionally nutrient-dense, emerald-fleshed fruit. Renowned for containing a massive concentration of Vitamin C that completely surpasses citrus alternatives, it provides unique protein-cleaving enzymes, rich fibers, and dense mineral metrics to drive gut motility and optimal defense.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: A low-to-moderate calorie whole food option that delivers dense physical hydration and exceptional cellular fuel.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains nominal structural plant proteins, though it is famous for housing actinidin—a unique protein-digesting enzyme.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Virtually fat-free, containing only trace healthy essential fatty acids embedded within its microscopic black edible seeds.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Composed of natural simple sugars managed efficiently by structural dietary fibers, resulting in a moderate glycemic response.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: An extraordinary mega-dose that exceeds the daily recommended allowance in a single serving, boosting systemic immunity and skin cell synthesis.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K1
microNutrients.description: An essential fat-soluble factor required for perfect blood coagulation mechanics and supporting the structural density of bone tissue.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: A robust blend of soluble and insoluble fibers that accelerates intestinal transit, feeds gut flora, and keeps glycemic curves smooth.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: A crucial cellular electrolyte that assists in fluid balance dynamics, nervous system electrical signaling, and healthy cardiac tone.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin E
microNutrients.description: A fat-soluble antioxidant rarely found in high amounts in low-fat fruits; it works alongside Vitamin C to halt lipid oxidation chains.

microNutrients.name: Lutein
microNutrients.description: Crucial plant pigment that deposits into the eye's macular area, absorbing harmful blue wavelengths and shielding ocular cell architecture.

microNutrients.name: Zeaxanthin
microNutrients.description: Works alongside lutein in the central retina, providing essential antioxidant coverage to shield photoreceptors from oxidative degradation.

healthBenefits: Elite Digestive Enhancement: Kiwi naturally produces *actinidin*, a highly functional protease enzyme that breaks down dense dietary proteins (like red meats or dairy), drastically speeding up gastric emptying and easing bloating.
Unrivaled Immune Fortification: Supplying over 100% of your daily Vitamin C value per 100g, kiwi drives rapid neutrophil leukocyte activity, helping guard systemic tissues from common pathogens.

Intestinal Motility & Regularity: The high water-binding capacity of kiwi's unique soluble and insoluble fibers softens the stool matrix and significantly optimizes bowel movement consistency without bloating.
Endothelial Vasodilation: The healthy presence of potassium and organic antioxidants aids in inhibiting blood platelet aggregation, helping manage lipid health and keeping blood pressure balanced.
precautions: High Allergenic Potential: Kiwi is a well-documented source of cross-reactive food allergens, primarily due to actinidin. Symptoms of a kiwi allergy include oral allergy syndrome (itching or tingling in the mouth and throat), hives, and in severe cases, anaphylaxis.

The Gelatin Cooking Conflict: Because actinidin aggressively breaks down protein molecules, using fresh raw kiwi in recipes containing gelatin or milk proteins will destroy the structure, preventing jello from setting or making dairy taste bitter.

Oral Mucosal Soreness: Consuming multiple raw kiwis at once can cause a temporary stinging or burning sensation on the tongue and inner cheeks. This is a harmless physical reaction caused by actinidin enzymes and microscopic needle-like calcium oxalate crystals (raphides) physically irritating the soft tissues.

Moderate Oxalate Content: Kiwi contains measurable amounts of natural organic oxalates. Individuals with a historical predisposition to calcium-oxalate kidney stone formations should regulate excessive intake.
